title: Expanded administrative penalty system for by-law tickets
subtitle: Dog licensing changes, privacy and workplace safety policies, digital services strategy, and community event updates.
overview: Council approved an Administrative Monetary Penalty System (AMPS) for all by-law infractions, extending the approach already used for parking tickets. Disputes will move from provincial court to an internal screening review, with an independent hearing officer as the next step. Council also approved the related by-law amendments and corporate policies {{vote:m7}}. Staff said this should shorten resolution times and make disputes easier for residents, and will report any budget adjustments in the 2024-2026 operating budget process.

On the consent agenda, Council approved amendments to the Animal Control By-law on dog licensing {{vote:m4}}, new privacy and records-disclosure policies {{vote:m5}}, and updated respectful workplace, workplace violence and health and safety policies {{vote:m6}}. Council received the Digital Services Strategy implementation report as information {{vote:m8}}; staff signalled that a request for more resources will come in the next budget cycle.

Council met in closed session before the public meeting, and the minutes report no decisions from it. The meeting ended with updates on community events and recognition of the Chief Administrative Officer's 20 years in municipal management.

decisions.detail: Council approved the General Administrative Penalty By-law, amendments to the Screening and Hearing Officer By-law and other by-laws, six AMPS corporate policies, and direction to report budget adjustments in the 2024-2026 budget process.
Council approved report COM2023-018 and amendments to the Animal Control By-law, related to dog licensing.
Council approved the Privacy Protection Framework Program Policy (A-039) and the Routine Disclosure and Active Dissemination of City Records Policy (A-040).
Council approved the Respectful Workplace, Workplace Violence, and Health and Safety Policy Statement policies and authorized the Mayor and CAO to sign them.
Council received report CORP2023-034 on implementing the Digital Services Strategy as information.

debate: Staff said court-based by-law tickets can take months to reach trial and can require time off work, while AMPS disputes can often be settled by email or phone. Staff said parking disputes now resolve faster than under the court process.

One councillor asked about equity concerns raised by community members. Staff replied that AMPS is more accessible, with virtual or in-person hearings. Staff also said they will involve equity and anti-racism staff in hearing officer recruitment and will look at restorative or mediation options.

Councillors asked how the policy against interfering in screening and hearings works. Staff said councillors can still ask staff about a ticket's options, but neither council nor staff should influence the outcome once it is in screening. Staff also said the work will mostly shift to handling inquiries, and the number of tickets is not expected to rise.

The Mayor asked for communications to remind residents about overnight parking passes. Staff said the City has developed AMPS jointly with Kitchener and Cambridge, so the process will be consistent across the region.

On digital services, councillors asked how new systems would fit with existing contracts and how residents would test services. Staff said they would favour vendors that work with the City's design system, and would use resident testing at each stage. One councillor noted that the strategy will need more funding in the next budget.
